extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, petitioners, patent owners, and counsel involved in AIA post-grant proceedings (IPR, PGR, CBM)
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance and procedural standards for instituting and conducting AIA-era patent proceedings (inter partes review, post-grant review, and covered business method reviews), including filing, service, timing, institution standards, motions to amend, discovery, joinder, and claim construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service at correspondence address of record
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioner must serve the patent owner at the correspondence address of record for the subject patent; service at any other address known to the petitioner as likely to effect service is permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once a patent has issued, correspondence addresses in the Office record may be unreliable; petitioner is required to serve at the correspondence address of record but may also serve at other addresses likely to effect service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic and EXPRESS MAIL® service (by agreement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon agreement of the parties, service may be made electronically, and service may be made by EXPRESS MAIL® or by means at least as fast and reliable as EXPRESS MAIL®. Personal service is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic service requires party agreement; service methods at least as fast and reliable as EXPRESS MAIL® are acceptable alternatives to personal service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date requirements for IPR petitions (§42.106)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to institute an inter partes review will not be accorded a filing date until the petition (1) complies with §42.104; (2) is served upon the patent owner at the correspondence address of record provided in §42.105(a); and (3) is accompanied by the fee set forth in §42.15(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These requirements implement 35 U.S.C. 312(a); petition must identify all real parties in interest and a copy must be provided to the patent owner or owner's representative.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-month window to correct defective petitions (IPR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioners have one month to correct defective petitions to institute an inter partes review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board will review petitions for procedural compliance and notify the petitioner if incomplete (e.g., failure to state the claims being challenged). The one-month correction period is subject to statutory limitations and does not cure statutory defects that prevent consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board procedural review and notice of incompleteness
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining whether to grant a filing date, the Board will review petitions for procedural compliance and notify petitioner of any non-compliance issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of procedural defects include failure to state the claims being challenged; notice will identify the defects so the petitioner can correct them within allowed time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner preliminary response allowed (IPR) (§42.107)
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner may file a preliminary response to the petition, consistent with 35 U.S.C. 313.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary response gives patent owner opportunity to set forth reasons why no inter partes review should be instituted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary response due date (IPR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Due no later than three months from the date of the notice that the request to institute an inter partes review has been granted a filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing earlier or filing a paper stating no response will be filed is permitted; no adverse inference is drawn if patent owner elects not to file or waives the response. The Board has three months from filing (or from the date such response was due) to determine whether to institute.

rubrics_metrics.name: No new testimonial evidence in patent owner preliminary response (IPR)
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner preliminary response is not allowed to present new testimony evidence (e.g., expert witness testimony on patentability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 35 U.S.C. 313 does not require presentation of testimonial evidence in a preliminary response; however, if additional discovery is authorized before filing the preliminary response, testimonial evidence obtained through that discovery may be submitted (for example when standing certification is challenged).

rubrics_metrics.name: No amendments in preliminary response (IPR)
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner preliminary response cannot include any amendment to the patent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motions to amend after institution are governed by §42.121; statutory disclaimers under 35 U.S.C. 253(a) in compliance with §1.321(a) are permitted and disclaimed claims will not be instituted for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution standard for IPR — reasonable likelihood (§42.108)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may not authorize an inter partes review to be instituted unless the Director determines that the information in the petition, and any patent owner preliminary response, shows there is a reasonable likelihood that the petitioner would prevail with respect to at least one of the claims challenged in the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reasonable likelihood standard is flexible and allows the judge room for exercise of judgment; the Board may take into account its ability to complete the proceeding timely (35 U.S.C. 316(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim-by-claim and ground-by-ground institution (IPR)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may authorize the review to proceed on all or some of the challenged claims and on all or some of the grounds of unpatentability asserted for each claim; it will identify the grounds upon which the review will proceed on a claim-by-claim basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any claim or issue not included in the authorization for review is not part of the review; institution notice will be published in the Official Gazette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board discretion to deny grounds prior to institution (IPR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to institution of a review, the Board may deny some or all grounds for unpatentability on some or all of the challenged claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denying grounds pre-institution is consistent with efficient administration of the Office and statutory considerations under 35 U.S.C. 316(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner response timing after institution (IPR) (§42.120)
rubrics_metrics.description: If no time for filing a patent owner response is provided in a Board order, the default time is three months from the date the inter partes review was instituted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three months is considered sufficient for a typical case and is consistent with the requirement that a final written decision be rendered within one year of institution (35 U.S.C. 316(a)(11)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions to amend standards and procedures (IPR) (§42.121)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and procedures for patent owner motions to amend: first motion need not be authorized by the Board and will be entered if it complies with timing and procedural requirements; additional motions require prior Board authorization; entry does not automatically result in entry into the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board regulates substitution of claims and amendments to control proliferation of issues and abuse and to ensure timely completion under 35 U.S.C. 316(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds to deny motions to amend (IPR)
rubrics_metrics.description: A motion to amend may be denied where the amendment does not respond to the ground of unpatentability involved in the trial, seeks to enlarge the scope of the claims, or introduces new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reflects statutory prohibitions (35 U.S.C. 316(d)(3)) against enlarging claim scope or introducing new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of reasonable number of substitute claims (IPR)
rubrics_metrics.description: A reasonable number of substitute claims is presumed to be one substitute claim per challenged claim, which may be rebutted by a demonstration of need.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This presumption aids efficiency and limits burden on the petitioner; the Board may allow more upon demonstration of need.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents required in a motion to amend (IPR)
rubrics_metrics.description: A motion to amend the claims must include a claim listing, show the changes clearly, and set forth: (1) the support in the original disclosure of the patent for each claim that is added or amended; and (2) the support in an earlier filed disclosure for each claim for which benefit of the earlier filing date is sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These requirements ensure amendments are supported by the original or earlier disclosures and prevent introduction of new matter or improper priority claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional motions to amend — good cause or joint request (IPR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional motions to amend may be permitted upon a demonstration of good cause by the patent owner or a joint request of the petitioner and the patent owner to materially advance a settlement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In considering good cause, the Board will consider impact on timely completion and additional burden on the petitioner; belated motions may impair the integrity and efficiency of the review and reduce petitioner's ability to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult Director before staying proceedings when statutory time runs (multiple proceedings/stays)
rubrics_metrics.description: When there is a question of a stay concerning a matter for which a statutory time period is running in one of the proceedings, it is expected the Director would be consulted prior to issuance of a stay, given the stay would impact the Office's ability to meet statutory deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: consult Director before staying an ex parte reexamination where the three-month statutory time period under 35 U.S.C. 303 is running.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joinder request timing
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner or petitioner may request joinder, but such a request must be filed no later than one month after institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a petition is accompanied by a request for joinder, §42.101(b) time periods do not apply; timeliness requirement is consistent with 35 U.S.C. 315(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental information filed after institution
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the institution of an inter partes review or post-grant review is based upon the information filed in the petition and any response, motions identifying supplemental information must be filed after the institution of the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental information is not the basis for institution (35 U.S.C. 314/324); Director's regulations establish procedures for filing supplemental information after petition filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-grant review is a trial subject to subpart A rules (§42.200(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A post-grant review is a trial and subject to the rules set forth in subpart A of title 42, Code of Federal Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PGR proceedings employ the same trial procedures as other AIA proceedings unless otherwise specified in subpart C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim construction standard in PGR and CBM — broadest reasonable interpretation (§42.200(b), §42.300(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim in an unexpired patent shall be given its broadest reasonable construction in light of the specification in which it appears.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is consistent with longstanding Office practice and is justified by the ability to amend claims in Office proceedings, which distinguishes them from district court proceedings (e.g., In re Yamamoto). Applies to PGR and CBM proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-year timeframe to final decision with six-month extension (PGR/CBM) (§42.200(c), §42.300(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: PGR and CBM proceedings have a one-year timeframe for administering the proceeding after institution, with up to a six-month extension for good cause; the one-year period may be adjusted in the case of joinder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This timing is consistent with statutory mandates (35 U.S.C. 326(a)(11)) and ensures timely resolution; Board may adjust for joinder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file a petition for post-grant review (§42.201)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who is not the patent owner may file a petition to institute a post-grant review, unless the petitioner or real party-in-interest had already filed a civil action challenging the validity of a claim of the patent (post-grant reviews are barred by prior civil action).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows 35 U.S.C. 325(a)(1) and prevents duplicative challenges; petitions may be barred by prior civil actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel bar for PGR petitions (§42.201(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition may not be filed where the petitioner, the petitioner's real party-in-interest, or a privy of the petitioner is estopped from challenging the claims on the grounds identified in the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent with 35 U.S.C. 325(e)(1) and 315(e)(1), estoppel attaches based on a final written decision in post-grant, CBM, or inter partes reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness requirement for PGR petitions — nine-month window (§42.202)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for a post-grant review must be filed no later than nine months after the grant of the patent or issuance of a reissue patent. For reissue patents, a petition cannot challenge a claim identical to or narrower than an original patent claim unless filed within nine months after the grant of the original patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This implements 35 U.S.C. 321(c) and is part of graduated early-window implementation for PGRs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director may limit number of PGRs during initial years (§42.202(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may limit the number of post-grant reviews that may be instituted during each of the first four one-year periods after post-grant review takes effect, although the Office does not expect to limit petitions at this time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reflects section 6(f)(2)(B) of the AIA allowing graduated implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee requirement for PGR petitions (§42.203)
rubrics_metrics.description: A fee must accompany a petition for post-grant review and no filing date will be accorded until full payment is received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent with 35 U.S.C. 322(a)(1); payment is a jurisdictional prerequisite to consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content specificity required in PGR petitions (§42.204(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition must identify each claim being challenged, the specific grounds on which each claim is challenged, how the claims are to be construed, how the claims as construed are unpatentable, why the claims as construed are unpatentable under the identified grounds, and exhibit numbers of the evidence relied upon with citations to the portions relied upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This level of particularity implements 35 U.S.C. 322(a)(3) and provides meaningful notice to the patent owner and the Board regarding the legal and factual basis for institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standing certification requirement in PGR petitions (§42.204(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: To establish standing, a petitioner must at a minimum certify that the patent is available for post-grant review and that the petitioner is not barred or estopped from requesting post-grant review; facially improper standing is a basis for denying the petition without reaching the merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents spuriously-instituted post-grant reviews and implements statutory standing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure to correct clerical/typographical mistakes in petition (§42.204(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner seeking to correct clerical or typographical mistakes in a petition may file a procedural motion to correct the mistakes; grant of such a motion would not alter the filing date of the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clerical corrections cannot be used to change substantive content that would affect the filing date or institution threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: PGR petition filing date requirements (§42.206)
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete petition will be accorded a filing date only when it identifies all real parties in interest, a copy is provided to the patent owner or representative, and it is accompanied by the fee established by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mirrors statutory requirements in 35 U.S.C. 322 and includes a one-month correction period for defective petitions unless the statutory deadline has passed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner preliminary response rules for PGR (§42.207)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owner may file a preliminary response due no later than three months from the notice that the request to institute a post-grant review has been granted a filing date; the preliminary response may not present new testimonial evidence and cannot include any amendment, but may include a statutory disclaimer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 35 U.S.C. 323 limits evidence in a preliminary response; if pre-response discovery is authorized, testimonial evidence obtained may be submitted. Although 35 U.S.C. 324 does not require Board to consider preliminary responses, Board expects to consider them in most cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution standard for PGR — more likely than not (§42.208)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may not authorize a post-grant review to be instituted unless the Director determines that the information in the petition, if unrebutted, demonstrates that it is more likely than not that at least one of the challenged claims is unpatentable; alternatively, institution may be based on a novel or unsettled legal question important to other patents or applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This implements 35 U.S.C. 324(a) and (b); institution may be claim-by-claim and ground-by-ground, and the Board may consider ability to complete the proceeding timely (35 U.S.C. 326(b)). Use of the novel-legal-question ground is expected to be rare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner response timing after institution (PGR) (§42.220)
rubrics_metrics.description: If no time for filing a patent owner response is provided in a Board order, the default time is three months from the date the post-grant review is instituted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This three-month default is considered sufficient and supports the goal of rendering a final decision within the one-year statutory period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions to amend standards and procedures (PGR) (§42.221)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and procedures for patent owner motions to amend in PGR mirror those in IPR: first motion need not be authorized and will be entered if it complies with timing and procedural requirements; additional motions require prior Board authorization; amendments may be denied if not responsive, enlarge scope, or introduce new matter; one substitute claim per challenged claim presumed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motions must include claim listings, changes shown clearly, and support in original/earlier disclosures. Additional motions may be allowed for good cause or joint request to materially advance settlement; Board will consider impact on timely completion and petitioner burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple proceedings and joinder rules (PGR) (§42.222)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a stay impacts the Office's ability to meet statutory deadlines, Director consultation is expected prior to issuance of a stay; joinder requests must be filed no later than one month after institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These rules mirror concerns in IPR about statutory deadlines and timely completion of reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental information rules for PGR (§42.223)
rubrics_metrics.description: Motions identifying supplemental information must be filed after the petition is filed because institution is based upon information in the petition and any response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows 35 U.S.C. 326(a)(3) and 324(a) to ensure institution decisions rest on the original petition and responses, not post-petition supplements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional discovery standard in PGR — good cause (§42.224)
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional discovery in a post-grant review is limited to evidence directly related to factual assertions advanced by a party, and the standard for additional discovery is good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interests-of-justice standard applies in IPRs and derivation proceedings and is slightly higher than good cause; good cause requires a party to show a specific factual reason justifying discovery, whereas interests-of-justice considers the totality of relevant circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: CBM proceedings follow PGR procedures with limited exceptions (§42.300)
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered business method patent review is a trial subject to the rules of subpart A and also subject to the post-grant review procedures in subpart C except for §§ 42.200, 42.201, 42.202, and 42.204.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBM proceedings largely follow PGR rules but with statutory exceptions; claim construction uses broadest reasonable interpretation and the one-year timing with six-month extension applies (adjustable for joinder).
